source.title: object.urlEncode() throws on a lone surrogate in the isolated-VM engine but not in the default one

source.body:
## Bug Description

`packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts` is a deliberate mirror of `packages/workflow/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts`, and its comment states the intent:

```ts
// DIVERGENCE from packages/workflow/src/extensions/object-extensions.ts:
// The original uses URLSearchParams which is a Web API unavailable inside the
// V8 isolate. encodeURIComponent is an ECMAScript built-in available in all
// V8 contexts, but it doesn't encode !'()~ which WHATWG requires. The extra
// replace step covers those characters to match URLSearchParams output.
```

They do not match for one input class. `URLSearchParams` replaces a lone surrogate with U+FFFD; `encodeURIComponent` throws a `URIError` on it. So the same expression succeeds on one engine and fails on another:

| | `{ v: "\uD800" }` |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/workflow` (URLSearchParams) | `v=%EF%BF%BD` |
| `@n8n/expression-runtime` (encodeURIComponent) | **throws `URIError`** |

## To Reproduce

A lone surrogate is easy to end up with — `JSON.parse` produces one from a `\uD800` escape, and so does slicing a string between the halves of a surrogate pair:

1. Create a workflow with a Code node returning `{ json: { payload: JSON.parse('{"a":"\\ud800"}') } }`.
2. In a following node use the expression `{{ $json.payload.urlEncode() }}`.
3. Run it with `N8N_EXPRESSION_ENGINE` set to the isolate-backed engine, then with the default one.

The default engine returns `a=%EF%BF%BD`. The isolate-backed engine raises `URIError: URI malformed`.

## Scope

I swept every BMP code point through both implementations, as key and as value, plus astral samples:

```
checked 65540 code points as both key and value
distinct disagreement shapes: 2

  workflow: v=%EF%BF%BD
  runtime:  URIError
  e.g. U+D800 as value, U+D801 as value, U+D802 as value, U+D803 as value

  workflow: %EF%BF%BD=x
  runtime:  URIError
  e.g. U+D800 as key, U+D801 as key, U+D802 as key, U+D803 as key
```

4096 disagreements out of 131,076 checks, all of them the 2048 surrogate code points in either position. Everything else is byte-identical, so `whatwgEncode` is right apart from this edge.

## Suggested fix

Make the string well-formed first, which is exactly what `URLSearchParams` does:

```diff
 function whatwgEncode(str: string): string {
-	return encodeURIComponent(str)
+	// URLSearchParams replaces lone surrogates with U+FFFD, while
+	// encodeURIComponent throws a URIError on them.
+	return encodeURIComponent(str.toWellFormed())
 		.replace(/%20/g, '+')
 		.replace(/[!'()~]/g, (c) => '%' + c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16).toUpperCase());
 }
```

With that applied the sweep reports **0 disagreements out of 131,076**. `String.prototype.toWellFormed` is ES2024 and available from Node 20; this repo requires Node >= 24.

## A second, related divergence

`packages/@n8n/expression-runtime/src/extensions/number-extensions.ts` carries a similar comment claiming parity:

```ts
// DIVERGENCE ... toLocaleString is an ECMAScript built-in available in all V8
// contexts and produces the same output.
```

`toLocaleString` and `Intl.NumberFormat.format` are indeed equivalent, but the mirror wraps the call in `try { ... } catch { return String(value) }`, and that is not. Where the original raises, the mirror returns the unformatted number:

| call | `packages/workflow` | `@n8n/expression-runtime` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `(1234.5).format('en-US', { style: 'currency' })` | throws `TypeError` | `1234.5` |
| `(1234.5).format('en-US', { minimumFractionDigits: 101 })` | throws `RangeError` | `1234.5` |
| `(1234.5).format('')` | throws `RangeError` | `1234.5` |

A malformed call is silently wrong on one engine rather than reported. I have not touched this one because the catch may be there for a limited-ICU isolate, which I cannot test from outside — happy to follow whichever way you want it to go.

## Operating System

macOS (reproduced against `master` sources directly)

## n8n Version

`master` at the time of writing

## Node.js Version

24

## Database

SQLite (default)

## Execution mode

main (default)

---

CONTRIBUTING.md asks for an issue before a bug-fix PR, so this is that. I have the `urlEncode` change ready with a regression test and will open a PR linking this issue — glad to hold off if you would rather triage first.
